R074-01.notes: Sisters both want the box, abandon Lena's split plan, agree to share it in rotation and laugh together for the first time since the hospital. A: no baking contest. C: grandmother is dead; no lessons. D: no cookbook copying.

R074-02.notes: P2: photograph every card, divide originals by category, each keep copies. A is the final arrangement (trap). B, D unsupported.

R074-03.notes: 'said that sounded fine, in the voice she used when nothing sounded fine' = unspoken disapproval. B: drive is mentioned but not linked to inattention. C is the opposite. D unsupported.

R074-04.notes: A 'Too salty—half next time', B 'Tried with honey. No.', C 'Better with the old oven' all quoted. No note about dividing the box; mother told them to sort it out.

flags.note: 'Spanning roughly six decades' requires assuming the story's present is the 2020s; the passage never dates the present. Plainly the best answer, but 'eleven dated entries spanning more than half a century' or simply 'from 1962 to two years ago' would be tighter.

R074-05.notes: Eleven dated entries from 1962 to two years ago. B contradicts (each changed something small). C, D unsupported.

R074-06.notes: 'She got it right every time... just kept trying to get it righter' = recipes already good, still improving. A is Ruth's view, rejected by Lena. C: no carelessness. D unsupported.

R074-07.notes: 'Almost delighted' plus 'famously confident cook' whose cards show constant revision = pleasure at finding she struggled too. A contradicts 'delighted'. B: no competition. D: cards are in her hand.

R074-08.notes: Order: A (P2), C (P4), B (P5), D (final paragraph, by evening).

R074-09.notes: Adding their own margin notes continues the grandmother's practice of revising and recording. B: adding, not replacing. C: no cookbook. D is the opposite.

R074-10.notes: Mother is 'tired of mediating' between the sisters, who both asked for the box = settling disputes. A, C, D don't fit the context; D is a trap based on Lena's sorting plan.

R074-11.notes: Last paragraph: youthful turning helps growth, fixed east-facing helps reproduction. B ignores the young-plant turning. C contradicted by the internal-clock finding. D contradicted by the rotated-pot result.

R074-12.notes: P2: east-side cells grow faster during the day, bending the top westward. A, C, D are not mentioned.

R074-13.notes: Plants kept swaying daily under a fixed light, so an internal clock is involved, not just the sun's position. A: they kept moving. B: no speed comparison. D unsupported.

R074-14.notes: P3: staked or rotated plants grew less. A, B, C are not stated; C draws on the pollinator material from P4.

R074-15.notes: P4: turning slows and then stops, and most flowers face east. B, C, D contradict this.

R074-16.notes: East-facing heads warmed faster and got about five times as many pollinator visits. A: seeds aren't mentioned and it reverses the pollinator finding. B is the opposite. D unsupported.

R074-17.notes: Warming west-facing heads separates warmth from direction; the warmed heads drew more pollinators, so morning warmth is the attractant. A, C, D aren't addressed by the setup.

R074-18.notes: The last paragraph summarizes 'not one behavior but two'. No new experiment (B), no denial (C), no discoverers (D).

R074-19.notes: 'Suspected that this orientation was not an accident' = not a chance result. A, B, C are other senses of the word that don't fit.

R074-20.notes: Stated outright in P2. A: Davis is in California, not the east. B, D unsupported.

R074-21.notes: 'A government decree intended to control public behavior helped create...' A: 'alone' contradicts 'forces outside art'. B: audiences valued artifice, not realism. D: no city rivalries.
